newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Three to share 1997 U.N. Population Award.
newsitem.headline: Three to share 1997 U.N. Population Award.

text.p: Population and family planning experts from El Salvador, Japan and Thailand were named on Wednesday as joint recipients of the 1997 U.N. Population Award.
It is presented annually to individuals and institutions that have made outstanding contributions to increasing awareness of population problems and their solutions.

This year's winners are: Elizabeth Aguirre Calderon Sol, director of the National Family Secretariat of El Salvador; Professor Toshio Kuroda, director emeritus of Nihon University Population Research Institute; and Sen. Mechai Veravaidya, director of Thailand's Population Development Association.
They will each receive a diploma, a gold medal and an equal share of the monetary prize of $25,000 at a ceremony later this year.
The prize has been awarded in the past to an individual, a single institution or both. Three laureates were chosen this year to mark the 15th anniversary of the award.

The winners were chosen by a committee, chaired by Ambassador Julio Armando Martini Herrera of Guatemala, and consisting of representatives of 10 U.N. members elected by the Economic and Social Council. U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, and the executive director of the United Nations Population Fund, Dr. Nafis Sadik, also serve as members.
